With the scrub, a release pipeline that exports AMA_INTEGRITY_REQUIRE_TRUST_ANCHOR=1 and runs `pip install .`/`python -m build` while the anchor is missing or mistyped now silently produces an UNANCHORED signed artefact instead of failing the build — a fail-open regression of a documented fail-closed switch (the docstring at setup.py:608-611 still lists the variable among what 'the signer reads', which is no longer true on this path). The legitimate deadlock the scrub solves (the signer child imports the package with the artefact stashed aside) could be solved without discarding the signing policy, e.g. by translating the parent's env var into a --require-trust-anchor argv flag. Mitigation: strict deployments that also set the variable at import time still fail at POST, and a pipeline that sets the anchor pubkey var is unaffected; the lost protection is the build-time typo/misconfiguration net.
